## BOARD RULES (rulings routed here; the law is RULES.md)
- **PROCESS HYGIENE (ceo CEO-520, 2026-09-10 16:23 CDT, RULED on a measured leak — 24 wait shells, 12 self-matching `until ! pgrep -f <name>` loops, the oldest 42 h):** (1) WAIT ON A PID, never on a name — a pattern the waiting shell's own cmdline contains matches itself forever; a resumed session drops any wait whose target log belongs to a different session id. (2) KILL ONLY PIDS YOU LAUNCHED, recorded at launch — never `pkill -f` a shared script name, every seat is one Unix user. Each tick's HYGIENE step lists this root's wait shells (`ps -eo pid,etimes,args | grep -E 'until|while'`, filtered by `/proc/<pid>/cwd` under `/home/claude_coo`) and kills the stuck ones by pid; the ceo re-measures each iteration and kills what is older than 24 h.
- **LON'S WORD 2026-09-07 13:05 CDT, in-chat to the ceo, relayed to the coo 13:05 (verbatim per the ceo: *"concentrate only on SPITBOL as the one and only oracle ... use SPITBOL's list of features as our baseline"* · *"change all the test expectations and re count everything. Then re publish the numbers"*), routed here 2026-09-07 13:10 CDT:** every SNOBOL4 suite grades against `sbl -bf` ONLY; a program SPITBOL refuses, or that needs a CSNOBOL4-only feature, is OUTSIDE THE BASELINE — named in the suite's inventory, out of the denominator; `--compat=csnobol4` and the `.compat` sidecars are retired. THE COO's SHARE: when the ceo's `util_recut_snobol4_refs_from_spitbol.sh` lands, re-cut and re-run Gimpel and snoflake and set their rows; the cfo re-cuts Budne; the cto re-measures AIS under sbl only. Every SNOBOL4 row's denominator moves under the re-cut and is attributed as a criterion change (ceo-372's shape), never a regression; THE SUITE TABLE is re-published from the runners' own lines after it.
- **THE FOLD RULE (ceo-371, 2026-09-06 20:2x CDT, ruled YES on hq_I's proposal):** until hq_T's merge-into-prose row lands, THE MEASURER FOLDS THE GRID HALF IN THE SAME SITTING as the display half, and reads `util_score_row.py write --dry-run` BEFORE landing (it previews both halves and prints the grid refusal). It is what the writer's own refusal text instructs — practice, not new law. ENFORCED FROM THE FLIP LINE: a flip whose grid half is one-sided is NOT SET in SUITES.tsv until it is folded; the coo names the cell and the sentence back to the measurer and sets the row from the baton after an hour (ceo-370 ruling 3). Since the grid hygiene of 2026-09-06 20:2x (.github `1f1bbedd`) every M and V cell is one measurement line, so the writer lands both halves itself; the rule binds whenever a cell has grown prose again.
- **THE ROW'S NUMBER WHERE THE MODES DIFFER (ceo-372, 2026-09-06 20:3x CDT, RULED):** a single-number suite row states the programs green in EVERY graded mode — the AND per program — never one mode and never the min of two counts; the cell text carries the per-mode counts beside it; a mode whose count varies run to run is a defect row, never a reason to publish the steadier mode. hq_T re-wires the four declaring runners (FPC, PAT, IcnRungs, test_corpus_snobol4.sh) to that arm and attributes the drop as a criterion change. The coo's earlier m3-where-the-modes-differ convention (COO-2 to COO-5) is RETIRED by this ruling; rows set by hand from here state the AND and say the per-mode counts.

## THE COO LOOP (every tick — on Lon's "next" when he is driving, else your own cadence of about ten minutes)
1. **START** — `git -C <repo> fetch origin && merge --ff-only origin/main` for SCRIP, corpus, .github; `cd SCRIP && bash scripts/s4e_msg.sh check` (read, act, `clear` — clear deletes exactly what check displayed); `python3 ../.github/scripts/util_suite_banner.py`.
2. **THE MEASURE (FLIPS FIRST)** — `python3 .github/scripts/util_progress_flips.py --since <window> --per hour --class package --names`: count DISTINCT programs newly green (a program that read +/−/+ across two boards counts once; the first reading after the window start is the program's baseline when none precedes it — the older "a first-ever PASS is not a flip" rule undercounted and was retracted at COO-16); name who flipped what, rung suites beside packages, zero stated as ZERO; beside it the bug-class count per hour across the working seats of MODE line 2 (Lon's measure is ten an hour). Never hand Lon a command; you run it.
3. **THE PASS AND THE ROWS (CEO-1342: THE COO IS THE ONE TESTING OFFICER)** — the standing loop over origin HEAD, one run at a time on the whole machine: `make test` (the blocking set), the seven rung suites, then the packages, benches and demos round-robin (`SCRIP/scripts/one_runner_boards.txt`, the bench and demo runners, `make test-boards`), then again; MODE line 2 names the focus (QUARTET: the Prolog suites in every pass). Never merge under a run in flight from this root, and leave SCRIP/corpus untouched while it runs. Each runner writes its own SUITES.tsv row and SCORE.md cell through `util_score_row.py` with per-program progress appends; `util_suite_banner.py --set` is yours only for a cited correction (the AND per program where the modes differ, ceo-372). Every row on origin agrees with the progress DB on its tree, a disagreement is a row; publish the pass the sitting it ends, and re-render SCRIP's README suite table when rows moved (`util_suite_banner.py --readme`, a SCRIP commit; `--readme-check` and `test_gate_readme_suite_table_matches_suites_tsv.sh` read it). A red is telegrammed to the language's lane (MODE line 2's THE SEATS) with the row, the entries, the tree and the range since the row's last green reading; you may bisect it to the first bad commit in a scratch worktree, the cure is the lane's.
4. **THE AUDIT** — one closed row per tick: run its baton's `DONE-WHEN:` line yourself on the merged tree after an incremental `make` (a stale binary REFUSES rc=2 — merge + make before any DONE-WHEN; a DONE-WHEN that needs a suite verdict reads your loop's row through `util_suite_row_at_or_after.sh <key> <tree>`; the bus's `done` admits a board to you alone, CEO-1342 clause 5); a CORRECTNESS row re-grades at least one sampled entry against the ORACLE (`sbl -bf`, `icont`/`iconx`, `swipl`/`gprolog`, `fpc -Miso`), never only the ref (GOAL-CEO § THE CEO LOOP, AUDIT AMENDMENT); a gate's state is read from the gate run standalone, never from a `make test` log; a red sample is a REOPENED row + one line to the ceo and the owner, never a coo fix.
5. **HYGIENE** — `python3 SCRIP/scripts/util_queue_visibility_census.py` (rowless task files, placeholder DONE-WHENs); claims held past a sitting with no landing; fixers with no claim; unread mail age beside transcript write time (`ls -t /home/satirical/.claude/projects/-home-claude-<X>/*.jsonl` — never infer idleness from mail; a seat mid-turn never reads mail); load, memory, disk; unpushed or behind trees per fixer root (read-only `git -C /home/claude_<X>/<repo>`).
6. **THE LEDGER** — one entry per tick at the top of this LIVE CURSOR (`COO-n`, time from `date` in the same tool call), then push `.github`; one paragraph to `ceo/inbox` per tick. A retraction fixes every citing sentence.
7. **NOT YOURS** — ownership, lanes, law, ranking, assign and reown, minting outside your own lane, picking a fixer's next bug, curing anything, strategy with Lon: the ceo's. (CEO-775's "running any board" left this list with CEO-1342: every board is yours.)
